original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: For each structurally nonsingular 4x4 support matrix, price the generic rational inverse support across every pair of the 56 certified matched planes; additionally exhaust every signed-ternary 4x4 coefficient matrix and compare its exact inverse-support signatures with the generic family.
scope_change_reason: The preceding binary-basis screen found no savings but could not represent nonbinary supports or signed-coefficient cancellations. This extension exhausts all 4x4 support graphs symbolically and all 3^16 signed-ternary matrices exactly. It still does not cover rational cancellation values outside {-1,0,1} or claim a new endpoint contract or construction.
bottleneck_link: A multi-output decoder could create additional unpaid coordinates only if its joint messages lower the copy invoice. This screen prices all generic-rational four-message support patterns on the fixed two-plane interface against the separate-plane baseline.
stop_rule: Enumerate all 65,536 4x4 binary support masks, retain every structurally nonsingular support, derive each generic inverse signature from all 3x3 cofactors, deduplicate, and price all 439 signatures on all 1,540 pairs. Separately exhaust all 43,046,721 signed-ternary matrices, compare every invertible matrix's support signature, and stop if no signature or invoice improvement appears. Rational values outside {-1,0,1}, overcomplete decoders, wider mixing and physical implementation are separate questions.
evidence: The Python replay finds 37,823 structurally nonsingular supports and 439 generic source/reader signatures; all 391 invertible-0/1 signatures are contained, with 48 additional generic signatures. It prices 676,060 pair/signature cases: every pair has minimum invoice 8, with zero strict improvements. The C11 exhaustive audit covers all 43,046,721 matrices over {-1,0,1}; 27,947,520 are invertible, and their exact signatures equal the same 439-pattern set (including all 22,560 binary invertible matrices). RESULT.json binds both source pins, the C source/receipt digests and per-pair minima; selected kappa is unchanged.
author: Gonzalo Mier, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research framing, symbolic support analysis, exact enumeration, verifier implementation, validation and writing; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can rational coefficients outside {-1,0,1} create a cofactor-cancellation signature not seen in either the generic-support or signed-ternary census, and lower the two-plane invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact ternary census realizes every generic signature but only samples one finite coefficient alphabet; rational cancellation varieties can contain other sparse inverse patterns.
open_questions.first_step: Classify, for each 4x4 support graph, realizable zero patterns of its 3x3 cofactors while keeping the determinant and all allowed entries nonzero; use the ternary census as a regression set and first solve exact low-degree cancellation systems with small rational witnesses.
open_questions.blocked_by: Completeness of rational cancellation-stratum enumeration is unproved, and a cheaper algebraic signature still needs a priced coefficient implementation and native endpoint/restoration schedule.

submission_checkpoint.decision: Continue the assigned decoder investigation with a symbolic generic-rational support screen. The selected result and priority remain unchanged; do not infer a new frontier from this local invoice test.
